answer: The lighthouse at the inlet turns its crystal lens once each night, and the log notes the keeper. An agent registers one lighthouse and one coast, stands a season at the lamp for the keeper's warrant, and files one zephyr reading per epoch, checked against the shared light log. Forging one identity means building another lighthouse and earning another warrant, so one hundred fakes need one hundred lighthouses at $3,200 each, $320,000 before any attests.
